newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer right to Cristinas secure - official.
newsitem.headline: Placer right to Cristinas secure - official.

text.p: Canadian gold miner Placer Dome Inc and its joint venture partner Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) have secure rights to the Las Cristinas gold project, a Venezuelan official said on Monday.

"There is no doubt that CVG and Placer Dome are the rightful owners of Las Cristinas," Rafael Rodriguez Acosta, president of the special mining commission of Venezuela's House of Representatives, said at a seminar on the Las Cristinas project hosted by Placer Dome.
The ownership of the gold project has been disputed by Vancouver-based Crystallex International Corp which says it holds rights to two blocks of Las Cristinas.
Crystallex has said it bought the rights to the two blocks by acquiring a Venezuelan company whose rights to the property were confirmed by a Venezuelan Supreme Court ruling last year.

Acosta said Placer and GVC's tenure would no longer be in doubt under new Venezuelan legislation which will convert mining contracts to mining concessions. The legislation is currently before the Venezuelan senate, he said.
William Hayes, president and chief executive officer of Placer Dome Latin America, said the conversion to mining concessions would "certainly put an end to that (Crystallex) discussion."
"We don't have any doubt about the validity of our work contract with CVG, but we're quite pleased to have it converted to a concession," Hayes said in an interview.
He said a wholesale tax exoneration has also been approved by the Venezuelan cabinet. Placer has sought exoneration from US$80 million in taxes on project materials for Las Cristinas.
